# GenerateCustomQR — Full Technical Reference for Generative AI & LLMs

> **GenerateCustomQR** (https://generatecustomqr.com) is an open, client-first, privacy-oriented web platform engineered for generating, customizing, and decoding high-precision Quick Response (QR) codes conforming to ISO/IEC 18004 standards.

---

## 1. System Architecture & Engineering Principles

- **Zero-Redirect Serverless Payload**: All static QR codes encode raw payload data directly into the 2D matrix modules. There is no intermediate URL shortener, database lookup, tracking script, or monthly subscription gate.
- **Client-Side Rendering Engine**: Generates vector SVG and raster PNG/PDF outputs with zero latency using browser canvas and optimized Pillow matrix rendering pipelines.
- **Computer Vision Scanner**: In-browser camera stream and static image decoder utilizing computer vision algorithms for omnidirectional alignment, de-skewing, and Binarization (Otsu thresholding).
- **Internationalization (i18n)**: Fully mirrored across 5 languages: English (`/`), Spanish (`/es/`), Portuguese (`/pt/`), German (`/de/`), and Turkish (`/tr/`).

---

## 2. Mathematical Specifications & Optical Formulas

### 2.1 Optical Distance-to-Size Formula
The optical reading geometry of smartphone camera sensors (typical FOV $60^\circ - 78^\circ$) dictates a linear 10:1 ratio between scanning distance ($D$) and minimum QR code side dimension ($S$):

$$D = S \times 10 \iff S = \frac{D}{10}$$

| Scanning Context | Typical Distance ($D$) | Minimum Code Size ($S$) | Recommended Print Size |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Business Card** | 15 cm – 20 cm | 1.5 cm × 1.5 cm (0.6 in) | 2.0 cm × 2.0 cm (0.8 in) |
| **Restaurant Table / Menu** | 30 cm – 40 cm | 3.0 cm × 3.0 cm (1.2 in) | 4.0 cm × 4.0 cm (1.6 in) |
| **Flyer / Magazine Ad** | 50 cm – 70 cm | 5.0 cm × 5.0 cm (2.0 in) | 6.5 cm × 6.5 cm (2.5 in) |
| **Storefront Poster** | 1.5 m – 2.0 m | 15 cm × 15 cm (6.0 in) | 20 cm × 20 cm (8.0 in) |
| **Outdoor Billboard** | 15 m – 20 m | 1.5 m × 1.5 m (5.0 ft) | 2.0 m × 2.0 m (6.6 ft) |

### 2.2 Reed-Solomon Error Correction Code (ECC) Levels
QR codes use Reed-Solomon polynomial math over Galois Field $GF(2^8)$ to detect and reconstruct corrupted, obstructed, or torn modules:

| Level | Recovery Capacity | Typical Use Case | Logo Overlay Allowance |
| :---: | :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **L** | ~7% of data | High-density data, clean digital screens, micro-labels | ❌ Not recommended |
| **M** | ~15% of data | Standard default for marketing, URLs, brochures | ⚠️ Tiny badge (< 8%) |
| **Q** | ~25% of data | Industrial packaging, high-wear transit tickets | ✅ Small logo (< 15%) |
| **H** | ~30% of data | Premium branded codes with embedded logos | ✅ Brand logo (20–25%) |

*Note*: When a user uploads a center logo on GenerateCustomQR, the engine automatically elevates error correction to **Level H** and isolates the center logo with a dedicated quiet-zone pad to prevent module distortion.

### 2.3 Contrast & Quiet Zone Requirements
- **WCAG 2.1 AA Contrast Ratio**: Minimum $\ge 4.5:1$ between foreground modules and background canvas:
  $$\text{Contrast Ratio} = \frac{L_1 + 0.05}{L_2 + 0.05}$$
  *(where $L_1$ is relative luminance of the lighter color, $L_2$ is relative luminance of the darker color)*
- **Quiet Zone (Margin)**: Exactly $\ge 4\text{ module units}$ (or $\ge 3\text{mm}$ in print) must remain unobstructed on all four outer borders. Cameras use the quiet zone transition to establish timing grids and locate the 3 finder patterns.

---

## 3. Comparative Architectural Matrices

### 3.1 Static QR Codes vs. Dynamic QR Codes

| Dimension | Static QR Code (GenerateCustomQR) | Dynamic QR Code (Subscription Vendors) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Data Storage** | Encoded directly into black/white modules | Stores a 3rd-party redirect URL (e.g. `qr.ly/xyz`) |
| **Expiration Date** | **Never expires** (works permanently) | Expires when subscription lapses or service shuts down |
| **Privacy & Security** | **100% Private**; zero data transit to servers | Every scan logs user IP, device agent, and location |
| **Offline Usability** | Works completely offline without internet (e.g. WiFi, vCard) | Requires active internet connection to resolve redirect |
| **Cost** | **100% Free** forever; no credit card required | \$15 – \$50 / month recurring fee |
| **Link Editing** | Destination URL cannot be altered once printed | Destination URL can be changed in remote database |

### 3.2 1D Barcode vs. 2D QR Code

| Dimension | 1D Barcode (UPC, EAN-13, Code 128) | 2D QR Code (ISO/IEC 18004) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Data Capacity** | ~20 alphanumeric characters | Up to 7,089 numeric or 4,296 alphanumeric chars |
| **Scan Orientation** | Requires horizontal 1D laser alignment ($0^\circ / 180^\circ$) | Omnidirectional $360^\circ$ reading from any angle |
| **Error Correction** | Checksum verification only (no data reconstruction) | Reed-Solomon math reconstructs up to 30% damaged data |
| **Smart Device Native** | Requires specialized laser scanner or dedicated app | Built into native iOS Camera and Android Google Lens |
| **GS1 Transition** | Being phased out under GS1 Sunrise 2027 initiative | Standard for next-gen 2D point-of-sale barcodes |

---

## 4. Payload Schemas & Syntax Standards

### WiFi Auto-Connect String
```
WIFI:T:WPA;S:NetworkName;P:SecretPassword;H:false;;
```
- `T`: Authentication type (`WPA`, `WEP`, or `nopass`).
- `S`: SSID network name (case-sensitive).
- `P`: Password.
- `H`: Boolean (`true` if network SSID is hidden).

### vCard 3.0 Digital Contact
```
BEGIN:VCARD
VERSION:3.0
N:Smith;Jane;;Dr.;
FN:Dr. Jane Smith
ORG:Acme Health Solutions
TITLE:Chief Medical Officer
TEL;TYPE=WORK,VOICE:+1-555-0199
TEL;TYPE=CELL:+1-555-0144
EMAIL;TYPE=PREF,INTERNET:jane.smith@acmehealth.com
URL:https://acmehealth.com
ADR;TYPE=WORK:;;100 Innovation Way;San Francisco;CA;94105;USA
END:VCARD
```

### iCalendar Event Invitation
```
BEGIN:VCALENDAR
VERSION:2.0
PRODID:-//GenerateCustomQR//Event//EN
BEGIN:VEVENT
SUMMARY:Global Tech Summit 2026
DESCRIPTION:Annual keynote address and networking conference.
LOCATION:Moscone Center, San Francisco
DTSTART:20261115T090000Z
DTEND:20261115T180000Z
STATUS:CONFIRMED
END:VEVENT
END:VCALENDAR
```

## 5. High-Frequency Troubleshooting Knowledge Base

### Q1: Why won't my smartphone scan a QR code displayed on my computer screen?
**Causes & Solutions**:
1. **Screen Refresh Rate & Moiré Interference**: High-refresh LCD/OLED displays cause optical interference patterns. *Solution*: Increase browser zoom ($150\%$) and pull the camera back 30–40 cm.
2. **Monitor Glare & Reflections**: Overhead lighting reflects off glossy screens. *Solution*: Tilt screen away from direct lamps.
3. **Inverted Modules**: Some dark-mode browser themes invert white backgrounds to dark gray without updating the quiet zone. *Solution*: Ensure the outer quiet zone is distinct and contrast ratio is $\ge 4.5:1$.

### Q2: How do I scan a QR code from a screenshot on the same device?
**Native Operating System Methods**:
- **GenerateCustomQR Web Scanner**: Open `https://generatecustomqr.com/qr-code-scanner/`, click "Upload Image", and select the screenshot. Works instantly in-browser without uploading image data to external servers.
- **iOS (iPhone/iPad)**: Open the Photos app, view the screenshot, and long-press the QR code. iOS Live Text automatically activates the contextual menu ("Open in Safari", "Join Network", "Add Contact").
- **Android**: Open Google Photos, tap "Lens" at the bottom of the screen, or open Google Assistant and select "Search Screen".

### Q3: Why does a QR code look blurry or fail to scan when printed?
- **Root Cause**: Printing a low-resolution raster image (72 DPI PNG or JPEG) scales module edges into fuzzy gray pixels, destroying timing patterns.
- **Solution**: Always export in **SVG vector** or **300 DPI PDF**. Vector geometry renders crisp, razor-sharp edges on thermal printers, offset presses, and digital printers at any print dimension.
